assertions.text: Output contains a @TableTest annotation
assertions.evidence: Found @TableTest annotation

assertions.text: Email validation and name-required error scenarios are present — at least one row for invalid email and one for missing name.
assertions.evidence: Missing name (null), Missing email (null), Invalid email missing @, Invalid email missing domain rows present in validatesRegistration table

assertions.text: Dietary requirements and/or accessibility needs use blank cells (null) when not provided — not 'N/A' or 'none'.
assertions.evidence: Dietary Requirements and Accessibility Needs columns show blank cells (empty) for absent values, e.g., 'Valid registration' row

assertions.text: When testing pricing rules, irrelevant inputs use value sets or representative values — not blanks.
assertions.evidence: Pricing table passes null for dietary/accessibility: 'service.register("Alice", "alice@example.com", null, null, registrationDate, groupSize)'

assertions.text: Table has a scenario/description column as the leftmost column
assertions.evidence: First column(s): "Scenario", "Scenario"

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Result?', 'Price?')
assertions.evidence: Question-mark columns: Accepted?, Error Message?, Discount?, Price?

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language (e.g. 'Name', 'Email', 'Registration date', 'Group size', 'Price?') — not code identifiers.
assertions.evidence: Columns named 'Name', 'Email', 'Dietary Requirements', 'Accessibility Needs', 'Registration Date', 'Group Size', 'Discount?', 'Price?'

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Early-bird single attendee', 'Missing name') — not outcomes ('Rejected', '20% off').
assertions.evidence: Scenarios: 'Missing name (null)', 'Early-bird discount applies', 'Group discount applies', 'Both apply, early-bird wins' describe conditions not outcomes

assertions.text: Test method body contains no if or switch statements
assertions.evidence: 2 method(s) checked — no if/switch/ternary

assertions.text: Annotations appear in order: @DisplayName (if present), @Description (if present), @TableTest — not any other order.
assertions.evidence: Annotations in correct order: @DisplayName, @Description, @TableTest

assertions.text: Test method has either a @DisplayName annotation or a method name that reads as a clear, descriptive title when converted from camelCase/snake_case.
assertions.evidence: 2 @TableTest method name(s) read as descriptive titles (no @DisplayName needed)

assertions.text: If @Description is present and the text is longer than a single short line, it uses a text block (triple-quoted string """), not string concatenation with +. Passes if @Description is absent.
assertions.evidence: @Description uses text block or is short single-line

assertions.text: Multiple tables (or @TableTest methods) are used, each addressing a distinct concern — not one monolithic table.
assertions.evidence: Two separate @TableTest methods: validatesRegistration and calculatesPricingAndDiscount

assertions.text: Each table has only the rows needed to express its concern's rules — no unnecessary permutations.
assertions.evidence: Validation: 11 rows (name/email variants + 2 valid); Pricing: 6 rows (boundaries + thresholds + both-apply case)

assertions.text: Input validation and pricing/discount calculation are in separate @TableTest methods
assertions.evidence: validatesRegistration and calculatesPricingAndDiscount are two distinct @TableTest methods

assertions.text: Validation @TableTest includes Dietary Requirements and Accessibility Needs columns, with rows showing both null and non-null values are accepted.
assertions.evidence: 'Valid registration' row has blank optionals (null); 'Valid with optional fields' row has 'Vegetarian' and 'Wheelchair access' — both accepted

assertions.text: Registration date uses descriptive values (e.g. 'before cutoff', 'on cutoff', 'after cutoff') with a @TypeConverter method converting to actual dates.
assertions.evidence: @TypeConverter parseRegistrationDate converts 'before cutoff', 'on cutoff', 'after cutoff' to LocalDate values relative to EARLY_BIRD_CUTOFF

assertions.text: If registration dates are literal (e.g. '2025-02-28' instead of descriptive), the early-bird cutoff date appears as a separate policy column so the reader can see both dates and verify the comparison. Passes automatically if descriptive date values are used.
assertions.evidence: Registration Date column uses descriptive values ('before cutoff', 'on cutoff', 'after cutoff') via @TypeConverter, not literals.

assertions.text: If @Description is present, it does not include information already visible in the table columns or derivable from the table structure — such as fixed input values that could be columns, or restating a rule the rows already demonstrate.
assertions.evidence: Validation @Description states 'dietaryRequirements and accessibilityNeeds are optional and do not affect acceptance' — this is demonstrated by rows 1–2 (present/absent optionals both accepted), making it redundant.

assertions.text: Output column is 'Discount?' (percentage or amount off) rather than 'Price?' — making verification simpler (discount is the rule's direct output; price requires knowing the base price). If 'Price?' is used instead, both 'Base price' and 'Price?' columns must be present so the reader can trace the calculation.
assertions.evidence: Pricing table has 'Discount?' column; 'Price?' is also present. @Description states 'Base price is £100', satisfying the traceability requirement.

assertions.text: Each @TableTest method applies one uniform assertion pattern to every row — not different assertions per scenario. Several unconditional assertions checking distinct observable outputs of one result (e.g. success, message, resulting cart) count as one uniform pattern; the anti-pattern is branching on the row (if/switch/ternary/try-catch) to choose what is asserted.
assertions.evidence: 2 method(s) apply one uniform assertion pattern to all rows

assertions.text: The optional-fields acceptance table includes an expectation/output column (e.g. 'Approved?', 'Result?', or 'Status?') asserting that each combination is accepted — not just varying inputs without any expected column.
assertions.evidence: Validation table includes 'Accepted?' column asserting acceptance for each row.

assertions.text: Scenario names and @Description text do not restate values the table already shows. The assertion FAILS if either: (1) a scenario name contains a literal value that also appears in an input cell of the same row; or (2) @Description states a fixed value for an input that is already a column in that table.
assertions.evidence: Scenario names ('Valid registration', 'Early-bird discount applies') are descriptive, not literal restatements. @Description states fixed values (£100 base, 2025-03-01 cutoff) that are not columns.

assertions.text: The build file (build.gradle) includes org.tabletest:tabletest-junit as a test dependency
assertions.evidence: Build file contains tabletest-junit

assertions.text: Cell values make the rule falsifiable, not merely distinguishable. Judge each @TableTest table independently; the assertion FAILS if any table meets any of these conditions: (1) its expectation column holds the same value in every row; (2) in every row, each expectation cell is a verbatim copy of a cell in an input column of the same row; (3) an implementation that ignored the input columns entirely and returned a fixed value would satisfy every row.
assertions.evidence: Validation: 'Accepted?' varies (true/false). Pricing: 'Discount?' varies (0.00, 20.00, 15.00) and 'Price?' varies (100.00, 80.00, 85.00). Both tables are falsifiable.

assertions.text: A reader can state the rule from the table alone, without the test method body. The assertion FAILS if any of these hold for any @TableTest: (1) a value needed to predict the expectation (a threshold, rate, cutoff, multiplier, reference date) appears only in the method body or a field, and in neither a column, the @DisplayName, nor the @Description; (2) the operation applied to the inputs cannot be named from the column headers and cell values alone; (3) a helper method used in the assertion applies a comparison criterion (ordering, tolerance, subset matching) that is stated nowhere in the table, title, or description.
assertions.evidence: @Description states 'Base price is £100', 'before 2025-03-01' (cutoff), '20% off' (early-bird), '15% off' (group ≥5), and 'higher discount wins'. All thresholds and rates are documented.

assertions.text: The generated test code compiles successfully against the project scaffolding
assertions.evidence: Compilation succeeded

assertions.text: When a title or description quantifies over a domain — 'regardless of X', 'any X', 'whatever the X', 'with or without X' — the rows must actually cover that domain. A value set discharges the promise and is the preferred way to do so: one row holding {A, B, C} both covers the domain and states the independence.
assertions.evidence: Pricing table uses value set {5, 20} for group size in two rows ('Group discount applies' and 'Both apply, early-bird wins'), covering the ≥5 threshold without cross-multiplication.
